chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man divorces his wife while he is absent, and proof is established for her that he divorced her in such and such a month, she observes her waiting period (iddah) from the day on which the divorce occurred with her husband; and if she does not remember that day, she observes the waiting period from the day she knows.
ai.seo_question: How does a woman observe her waiting period if her husband is absent and the exact day of divorce is unknown?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural mechanics of iddah when the husband is absent, prioritizing the known date of the actual pronouncement over the date of notification. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between the effective date of the divorce (talaq) and the date of its awareness, ensuring fairness in the waiting period calculation. This ruling is foundational in fiqh al-mara'ah for cases of delayed notification or travel.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man divorces and he is absent, so the proof is established for her that he divorced her during such and such a month, she would observe her waiting period from the day which therein was the divorce from her husband; and if she has not memorised that day, she would observe the waiting period from the day she knows’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘If a man divorces his wife when he is absent and testimony is established to prove the date of such divorce, she can commence her ‘Iddah (waiting period) from the day her husband had divorced her. If it is not proved then she must commence her ‘Iddah (waiting period) from the time she is informed.’”
